To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we used experimentally defined pathways to represent the multifunctionality of genes and proteins in a network, and that the resulting network revealed the interdependent relationships between pathways and the modular organisation of biological processes.
we have used a novel approach to identify functionally related pathways and that this approach has revealed the cooperation of multiple functional modules in biological processes.
the pathway network reveals the cooperation of multiple biological pathways and their organisation into functionally related modules with interdependent outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organisation of biological processes, and how this organisation can be used to improve our understanding of gene/protein function.
the organisation of molecular function, as a means to better understand biological processes and their regulation.

the disentangling of the multifunctional nature and pleiotropic effects of molecular function, in order to provide a better understanding of the biological processes that occur at the molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathway network provides a novel way to analyse and understand biological systems.
the pathway network provides a new way of viewing biological processes and the genes/proteins that participate in them.
the pathway network provides a new way to view biological processes, and may be useful to identify novel functional relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our pathway network provides a framework for the study of molecular function in a spatial/temporal context.
we have developed a method for the disentanglement of molecular function, and that the resulting pathway network provides a new framework for understanding biological function and its regulation.
we have shown how the multigenic, pleiotropic nature can be used to organise and understand biological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network of pathways is more informative than the network of genes or proteins, and it can be used to better understand the biological systems.
the organisation of pathways is not random and that the organisation is a reflection of the underlying biology.
a network-based approach can be used to organise pathways according to their functional relationships, providing a framework for analysing the interdependence of biological processes.
